![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224622/assets/8957a7db313379597a21e6b51d6c4493058af207a2d8edd5fafb8e549ba45aae.png)

Consider the finite region bounded by the curves $x=1+y$ and $x=1+{y}^{3},$ as shown above. Find an integral expression for the volume generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
First, let $f(y)=1+y$ and $g(y)=1+{y}^{3}.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y) & =g(y) \\ 1+y & =1+{y}^{3} \\ y-{y}^{3} & =0 \\ y(1-{y}^{2}) & =0 \\ y(1-y)(1+y) & =0 \\ y & =-1,0,1\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions corresponding to our region are $y=0$ and $y=1.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=0$ to $y=1.$ 

Now, let's draw our usual horizontal arrow through the region to determine the left and right functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224622/assets/b91dedd1282ce1e9d8546bc6f7c52eba8741a2cd49613a03ef62866a9ba91b0c.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the left function $x=g(y)=1+{y}^{3},$ and

- *leaves* through the right function $x=f(y)=1+y.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}y([\text{right}]-[\text{left}])\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}y([1+y]-[1+{y}^{3}])\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}y(y-{y}^{3})\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$
